description: Manually authored QA set over sample_docs/rag_primer.pdf, a 4-page original primer on Retrieval-Augmented Generation written for this project. Each answerable question lists the page(s) that should be retrieved as ground truth for retrieval metrics.

items.question: What is Retrieval-Augmented Generation?
items.expected_answer: RAG is a technique that combines a retrieval system searching an external knowledge base with a large language model that generates answers, rather than relying only on what the model memorized during training.

items.question: Where was the idea of RAG first popularized, and by whom?
items.expected_answer: In a 2020 paper by researchers at Facebook AI Research, showing that a neural retriever combined with a sequence-to-sequence generator produced more accurate, verifiable answers.

items.question: What are the main stages of a RAG pipeline?
items.expected_answer: Document ingestion and text cleaning, chunking, embedding generation, vector storage, and retrieval.

items.question: Why is it important to use the same embedding model for both queries and document chunks?
items.expected_answer: So that semantically similar pieces of text end up close together in the same vector space, which is necessary for similarity search to work correctly.

items.question: Why does RAG reduce hallucination compared to a standalone LLM?
items.expected_answer: Because the model's attention is constrained to a small set of relevant retrieved passages instead of relying purely on memorized training knowledge, and it is instructed to say when the context is insufficient rather than guess.

items.question: What metrics are used to evaluate a RAG system's retrieval quality?
items.expected_answer: Hit Rate at K, Recall at K, and Precision at K.

items.question: What two properties are typically assessed when evaluating generation quality?
items.expected_answer: Correctness (does the answer match the expected answer in substance) and faithfulness/groundedness (is every claim supported by the retrieved context).
